intro: Hi! In this lesson you learn words to talk about your work, your studies and the technology you use every day: meetings and deadlines, exams and homework, apps and passwords. Warm-up: do you work or study, and which app do you open first in the morning?
teachingNotes: Teach the words in small themed groups with an Indonesian gloss: work (meeting, report, deadline, colleague, manager, office, factory, shift, work from home), school and university (subject, class/lesson, homework, test/exam, semester, lecturer, degree, thesis), technology (email, app, password, download/upload, log in, attach a file, click). Practise them in short simple present and present continuous sentences with Indonesian contexts (kantor, pabrik, kampus, skripsi, UTBK). The learner already knows the jobs and workplaces of a1-vocab-jobs-hobbies (teacher, nurse, office worker, work in an office/factory): build on them, don't reteach them.

Common error: *'I work as accountant' (from 'bekerja sebagai akuntan', no 'seorang'). One job needs a/an, also after 'as': I work as an accountant, a receptionist, an engineer. Remind: an before a vowel SOUND, a university lecturer (a: 'yu' sound). Contrast work as (job), work in/at (place), work for (company).

Common error: *'I have many homeworks'. Homework is uncountable (like rice and water from A1): no a/an, no -s; say a lot of homework (a lot of = banyak, a phrase to remember), How much homework?, I don't have any homework. 'work' (pekerjaan) is uncountable too. You DO homework, not *make. 'assignment' is countable (two assignments) if a learner asks why.

Common error: *'I can't login'. The verb is two words, log in (I log in, she logs in, log out); 'login' is one word only as a noun or before a noun (the login page, login details). Sign in = log in. download = internet → phone, upload = phone → internet.

False friends and traps: pabrik = factory (fabric = kain); skripsi = thesis (a script = naskah); have a meeting, write a report (not *make a meeting). British vs American: lecturer (UK) / professor (US), at university (UK) / in college (US), maths / math, favourite / favorite.

Limits: A1 grammar only: simple present, present continuous, can/can't, there is/are, imperatives, like, some/any. No past simple (say 'I can't remember my password', not 'I forgot'), no will, no have to (use the simple present or imperatives), no present perfect. If a learner uses those, accept them but don't teach them here.

keyPoints.title: Tasks and places at work
keyPoints.explanation: Talk about your work day: have a meeting, write a report, finish before the deadline, work with colleagues and your manager, work in an office or a factory, work the night shift, work from home. Say your job with work as a/an: I work as an accountant.

material.title: At work: people, tasks and places

id.title: Di tempat kerja: orang, tugas dan tempat

blocks.text:
You already know jobs and workplaces (*I'm a nurse. I work in a hospital.*). Now let's talk about what happens at work.
- **People:** your **manager** (your boss, the person who leads your team) and your **colleagues** (the people you work with). *Colleague* is said 'KOL-iig'.
- **Tasks** (tugas, the things you do): **have a meeting**, **write a report**, **answer emails**, **finish before the deadline** (the last day or time to finish a task).
- **Places and times:** work **in an office** (kantor) or **in a factory** (pabrik), **work from home** (WFH), work **the morning shift** or **the night shift** (sif, your working hours when a place is open day and night).

id.text:
Kamu sudah tahu nama pekerjaan dan tempat kerja (*I'm a nurse. I work in a hospital.*). Sekarang kita bicara tentang apa yang terjadi di tempat kerja.
- **Orang:** **manager** kamu (atasan, orang yang memimpin timmu) dan **colleagues** kamu (rekan kerja, orang yang bekerja bersamamu). *Colleague* dibaca 'KOL-iig'.
- **Tugas** (hal-hal yang kamu kerjakan): **have a meeting** (ada rapat), **write a report** (membuat laporan), **answer emails** (membalas email), **finish before the deadline** (selesai sebelum tenggat waktu, yaitu hari atau jam terakhir untuk menyelesaikan tugas).
- **Tempat dan waktu:** kerja **in an office** (di kantor) atau **in a factory** (di pabrik), **work from home** (WFH, kerja dari rumah), kerja **the morning shift** atau **the night shift** (sif pagi / sif malam, yaitu jam kerjamu di tempat yang buka siang dan malam).

rows.en: I have a meeting with my manager at ten.
rows.id: Saya ada rapat dengan atasan saya jam sepuluh.

rows.en: Budi is writing a report for the meeting.
rows.id: Budi sedang membuat laporan untuk rapat.

rows.en: The deadline is Friday at 5 p.m.
rows.id: Tenggat waktunya hari Jumat jam 5 sore.

rows.en: My colleagues and I have lunch at a warung near the office.
rows.id: Saya dan rekan-rekan kerja makan siang di warung dekat kantor.

rows.en: Pak Joko works in a factory in Bekasi. This week he's on the morning shift.
rows.id: Pak Joko bekerja di pabrik di Bekasi. Minggu ini dia masuk sif pagi.

rows.en: On Fridays I work from home.
rows.id: Setiap hari Jumat saya kerja dari rumah.

blocks.text:
Watch out for these traps:
- **pabrik = factory**, not *fabric*. In English, **fabric** means kain.
- Say **write a report** (membuat laporan) and **have a meeting** (ada rapat). 'Make a meeting' is wrong.
- **work from home** has no *the* and no *my*: *I work from home on Mondays.* *WFH* is fine in chat messages too.
- **boss** is relaxed; **manager** is the name of the job. Both are fine for *atasan*.

id.text:
Hati-hati dengan jebakan ini:
- **pabrik = factory**, bukan *fabric*. Dalam bahasa Inggris, **fabric** artinya kain.
- Katakan **write a report** (membuat laporan) dan **have a meeting** (ada rapat). 'Make a meeting' salah.
- **work from home** tanpa *the* dan tanpa *my*: *I work from home on Mondays.* *WFH* juga boleh di pesan chat.
- **boss** lebih santai; **manager** adalah nama jabatannya. Dua-duanya bisa untuk *atasan*.

blocks.prompt: Our ___ is at 9 a.m. in the big room. The whole team comes.
blocks.explain: A meeting (rapat) is when people come together to talk. A deadline is the last time to finish a task, and a report is a document you write: nobody 'comes' to them.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Our ___ is at 9 a.m. in the big room. The whole team comes.
id.explain: Meeting (rapat) adalah saat orang berkumpul untuk berbicara. Deadline adalah batas waktu menyelesaikan tugas, dan report adalah dokumen yang kamu tulis: orang tidak 'datang' ke sana.

material.title: I work as an accountant: don't forget a/an

id.title: I work as an accountant: jangan lupa a/an

blocks.text:
To say your job, use **I'm a/an** + job, or **I work as a/an** + job (bekerja sebagai). Indonesian says *Saya bekerja sebagai akuntan*, with no *seorang*, so learners often drop the article. But English needs **a** or **an** before one job, also after **as**: **I work as an accountant**, never 'I work as accountant'.

Remember how to choose: **an** before a vowel sound (*an accountant, an engineer, an office manager*), **a** before a consonant sound (*a receptionist, a programmer*). For more than one person, use the plural and no a/an: *They work as accountants.*

id.text:
Untuk menyebut pekerjaanmu, pakai **I'm a/an** + pekerjaan, atau **I work as a/an** + pekerjaan (bekerja sebagai). Bahasa Indonesia bilang *Saya bekerja sebagai akuntan* tanpa *seorang*, jadi banyak orang lupa a/an. Tapi bahasa Inggris butuh **a** atau **an** sebelum satu pekerjaan, juga setelah **as**: **I work as an accountant**, bukan 'I work as accountant'.

Ingat cara memilihnya: **an** sebelum bunyi vokal (*an accountant, an engineer, an office manager*), **a** sebelum bunyi konsonan (*a receptionist, a programmer*). Untuk lebih dari satu orang, pakai bentuk jamak (plural) tanpa a/an: *They work as accountants.*

rows.en: My sister works as an engineer.
rows.id: Kakak saya bekerja sebagai insinyur.
rows.note: an: 'en-ji-NIR' starts with a vowel sound

rows.en: Dimas works as a programmer in Jakarta.
rows.id: Dimas bekerja sebagai programmer di Jakarta.

rows.en: Pak Hasan works as a university lecturer.
rows.id: Pak Hasan bekerja sebagai dosen.
rows.note: a: university is said 'YU-ni-ver-si-ti', a 'y' sound

rows.en: Rina and Sari work as nurses.
rows.id: Rina dan Sari bekerja sebagai perawat.

id.note: dua orang: bentuk jamak, tanpa a/an

blocks.text:
Three small words, three meanings:
- **work as** + a job: *I work as an accountant.*
- **work in / at** + a place: *I work in an office. I work at a bank.*
- **work for** + a company or a person: *She works for a big company.*

id.text:
Tiga kata kecil, tiga arti:
- **work as** + pekerjaan: *I work as an accountant.* (bekerja sebagai)
- **work in / at** + tempat: *I work in an office. I work at a bank.* (bekerja di)
- **work for** + perusahaan atau orang: *She works for a big company.* (bekerja untuk / di perusahaan)

blocks.explain: One job needs a/an, also after 'as': works as a programmer. Programmer starts with a consonant sound, so 'a'. 'is work' mixes two verbs.

id.explain: Satu pekerjaan butuh a/an, juga setelah 'as': works as a programmer. Programmer diawali bunyi konsonan, jadi 'a'. 'is work' mencampur dua kata kerja.

blocks.text:
Words for school and campus:
- **subject**: mata pelajaran (school) / mata kuliah (university): *maths, biology, accounting*.
- **class** or **lesson**: jam pelajaran / kelas: *I have an English class at eight.* Both words are fine here.
- **test** and **exam**: a **test** is short (ulangan, kuis); an **exam** is big (UAS, the UTBK). You **take** an exam and you want to **pass** it (lulus).
- **semester**: *I'm in my fifth semester* (semester 5).
- **lecturer**: dosen. At school you have a **teacher**; at university you have a **lecturer**.
- **degree**: gelar: *a degree in economics*. S1 is a **bachelor's degree**.
- **thesis**: skripsi. Said 'THII-sis', with *th* as in *think*.

id.text:
Kata-kata untuk sekolah dan kampus:
- **subject**: mata pelajaran (sekolah) / mata kuliah (kuliah): *maths, biology, accounting*.
- **class** atau **lesson**: jam pelajaran / kelas: *I have an English class at eight.* Dua-duanya benar di sini.
- **test** dan **exam**: **test** itu pendek (ulangan, kuis); **exam** itu besar (UAS, UTBK). Kamu **take** an exam (ikut ujian) dan ingin **pass** (lulus).
- **semester**: *I'm in my fifth semester* (semester 5).
- **lecturer**: dosen. Di sekolah ada **teacher** (guru); di kampus ada **lecturer** (dosen).
- **degree**: gelar: *a degree in economics*. S1 adalah **bachelor's degree**.
- **thesis**: skripsi. Dibaca 'THII-sis', *th* seperti di *think*.

rows.en: My favourite subject is biology.
rows.id: Mata pelajaran favorit saya biologi.

rows.en: We have a maths test every Friday.
rows.id: Kami ada ulangan matematika setiap hari Jumat.

rows.en: Rina is in her sixth semester. She's writing her thesis.
rows.id: Rina semester enam. Dia sedang menulis skripsi.

rows.en: Our lecturer is very kind.
rows.id: Dosen kami sangat baik.

rows.en: My brother has a degree in accounting.
rows.id: Kakak saya punya gelar di bidang akuntansi.

blocks.text:
**skripsi** is not *script*: a **script** is the text of a film or a play (naskah). Skripsi is a **thesis**.

British and American: a university teacher is a **lecturer** in British English and usually a **professor** in American English. Americans also say **college** for university: *I'm in college* = *I'm at university*.

id.text:
**skripsi** bukan *script*: **script** adalah naskah film atau drama. Skripsi adalah **thesis**.

Inggris (UK) dan Amerika (US): dosen disebut **lecturer** dalam bahasa Inggris British, dan biasanya **professor** dalam bahasa Inggris Amerika. Orang Amerika juga bilang **college** untuk universitas: *I'm in college* = *I'm at university* (saya kuliah).

blocks.prompt: At the end of the semester, students take a big ___ in every subject.
blocks.explain: You take an exam (ujian) at the end of the semester. A lesson is a normal class, and a degree is what you get at the end of university.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: At the end of the semester, students take a big ___ in every subject.
id.explain: Kamu take an exam (ikut ujian) di akhir semester. Lesson adalah jam pelajaran biasa, dan degree adalah gelar yang kamu dapat di akhir kuliah.

material.title: Homework: no -s, and you do it

blocks.text:
**homework** (PR, tugas rumah) is an **uncountable** noun, like *rice* and *water*: a word for a thing we don't count one by one. So it has **no a/an** and **no -s**: 'a homework' and 'homeworks' are wrong. The word **work** (pekerjaan) works the same way: *I have a lot of work today.*

To say *banyak PR*, use **a lot of homework**. *A lot of* means banyak: it's a phrase to remember, and it goes with both kinds of nouns (*a lot of books, a lot of homework*). To ask, use **How much homework …?**, and in negatives **any**: *Sari doesn't have any homework.*

And you **do** homework (mengerjakan PR), you don't 'make' it.

id.text:
**homework** (PR, tugas rumah) adalah kata benda **uncountable** (tidak bisa dihitung), seperti *rice* dan *water*: kata untuk benda yang tidak kita hitung satu per satu. Jadi **tanpa a/an** dan **tanpa -s**: 'a homework' dan 'homeworks' salah. Kata **work** (pekerjaan, kerjaan) juga begitu: *I have a lot of work today.*

Untuk bilang *banyak PR*, pakai **a lot of homework**. *A lot of* artinya banyak: ungkapan untuk diingat saja, dan bisa dipakai dengan dua jenis kata benda (*a lot of books, a lot of homework*). Untuk bertanya, pakai **How much homework …?**, dan di kalimat negatif pakai **any**: *Sari doesn't have any homework.*

Dan PR itu di-**do** (mengerjakan PR), bukan 'make'.

rows.en: Our lecturer gives us a lot of homework.
rows.id: Dosen kami memberi kami banyak tugas.

rows.en: Budi does his homework at the library.
rows.id: Budi mengerjakan PR-nya di perpustakaan.

rows.en: Do you have any homework for tomorrow?
rows.id: Kamu ada PR untuk besok?

rows.en: I have two assignments this week.
rows.id: Saya punya dua tugas minggu ini.

blocks.text: Why *two assignments* but not *two homeworks*? Because **assignment** (one task from your lecturer) is countable and **homework** is not. That's English, not logic: just remember it. In Indonesian *banyak PR* has no plural either, so the trap comes from adding the -s.

id.text: Kenapa *two assignments* tapi bukan *two homeworks*? Karena **assignment** (satu tugas dari dosen) bisa dihitung (countable) dan **homework** tidak. Itu aturan bahasa Inggris, bukan logika: cukup diingat. Di bahasa Indonesia *banyak PR* juga tidak berbentuk jamak, jadi jebakannya justru saat menambahkan -s.

blocks.prompt: Our teacher gives us ___ every weekend.
blocks.explain: Homework is uncountable: no a/an and no -s. Use a lot of homework for banyak PR.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Our teacher gives us ___ every weekend.
id.explain: Homework tidak bisa dihitung (uncountable): tanpa a/an dan tanpa -s. Pakai a lot of homework untuk banyak PR.

material.title: Technology: email, app, password, log in

id.title: Teknologi: email, app, password, log in

blocks.text:
Many technology words are the same in Indonesian, so they're easy: **email**, **app** (aplikasi, short for *application*), **password** (kata sandi), **file**, **click** (klik). Learn them in phrases:
- **send an email**, **open the app**, **click the link**, **type your password**
- **download** (unduh: from the internet to your phone) and **upload** (unggah: from your phone to the internet)
- **attach a file** (melampirkan file) to an email
- **on my phone**, **on my laptop** (di HP, di laptop)

Use **an** with *an email* and *an app* (vowel sound), but **a** with *a password* and *a file*.

id.text:
Banyak kata teknologi sama dengan bahasa Indonesia, jadi gampang: **email**, **app** (aplikasi, kependekan dari *application*), **password** (kata sandi), **file**, **click** (klik). Pelajari dalam frasa:
- **send an email** (kirim email), **open the app** (buka aplikasinya), **click the link** (klik tautannya), **type your password** (ketik kata sandimu)
- **download** (unduh: dari internet ke HP-mu) dan **upload** (unggah: dari HP-mu ke internet)
- **attach a file** (melampirkan file) ke email
- **on my phone**, **on my laptop** (di HP, di laptop)

Pakai **an** untuk *an email* dan *an app* (bunyi vokal), tapi **a** untuk *a password* dan *a file*.

rows.en: log in
rows.id: masuk ke akun

rows.en: I can't log in because I can't remember my password.
rows.id: Saya tidak bisa masuk karena saya lupa kata sandi saya.

rows.en: Rina logs in to the app every morning.
rows.id: Rina masuk ke aplikasi itu setiap pagi.

rows.en: the login page
rows.id: halaman login
rows.note: noun or before a noun: one word

id.note: kata benda atau sebelum kata benda: satu kata

rows.en: Please attach your CV to the email.
rows.id: Tolong lampirkan CV-mu ke email.

blocks.text: **log in** (two words) is the action: *I log in, she logs in, I can't log in, Log in here.* **login** (one word) is a thing or goes before a thing: *the login page, your login details.* Indonesian writes *login* for both, so learners write 'I can't login'. The opposite is **log out**. **Sign in** means the same as *log in*.

id.text: **log in** (dua kata) adalah tindakannya: *I log in, she logs in, I can't log in, Log in here.* **login** (satu kata) adalah benda atau dipakai sebelum benda: *the login page, your login details* (data login-mu). Bahasa Indonesia menulis *login* untuk keduanya, jadi banyak orang menulis 'I can't login'. Lawannya **log out**. **Sign in** artinya sama dengan *log in*.

options: Please log in with your email.
blocks.explain: Here it's an action (a verb), so it's two words: log in. 'login' as one word is only for a thing, like the login page.

id.explain: Di sini log in adalah tindakan (kata kerja), jadi dua kata: log in. 'login' satu kata hanya untuk benda, misalnya the login page.

resources.note: A2 picture, matching and gap-fill exercises with more job words (manager and others). Good extra practice for the work part.

id.note: Latihan gambar, mencocokkan dan isian tingkat A2 dengan lebih banyak nama pekerjaan (manager dan lainnya). Bagus untuk latihan tambahan bagian kerja.

resources.title: Let's Learn English! Topic: College and University
resources.source: Learn English with Bob the Canadian
resources.note: Bob talks slowly about words and phrases for college and university. He uses North American words (college, professor), and the video is a little above this lesson's level.

id.note: Bob berbicara pelan tentang kata dan frasa untuk kuliah. Dia memakai kata-kata Amerika Utara (college, professor), dan videonya sedikit di atas level pelajaran ini.

resources.title: Learn English - Internet Vocabulary
resources.note: Alex explains common internet words, like sign in and sign up. It covers more words than this lesson and is a little above A2.

id.note: Alex menjelaskan kata-kata internet yang umum, seperti sign in dan sign up. Kata-katanya lebih banyak dari pelajaran ini dan sedikit di atas A2.

id.intro: Hai! Di pelajaran ini kamu belajar kata-kata untuk membicarakan pekerjaanmu, kuliah atau sekolahmu, dan teknologi yang kamu pakai setiap hari: rapat dan tenggat waktu, ujian dan PR, aplikasi dan kata sandi. Pemanasan: kamu kerja atau kuliah, dan aplikasi apa yang pertama kamu buka di pagi hari?

assessment.wks-1: Tulis dalam bahasa Inggris: Paman saya bekerja sebagai guru bahasa Inggris.
assessment.wks-2: Rina bekerja di pabrik. Minggu ini dia mulai kerja jam 10 malam dan selesai jam 6 pagi. Lengkapi: She's on the night ___.
assessment.wks-3: Dengarkan Dimas. Di mana dia bekerja setiap hari Senin dan Jumat? Jawab dalam bahasa Inggris.
assessment.wks-4: Tulis dalam bahasa Inggris: Saya tidak punya PR hari ini.
assessment.wks-5: Lengkapi dengan do atau make: I always ___ my homework after dinner.
assessment.wks-6: Perbaiki kesalahannya: Sari can't login because her password is wrong.
assessment.wks-7: Lengkapi dengan download atau upload: The form is on our website. Please ___ it and print it.
